_comment: THE EXAMPLES ARE TYPECHECKED, AND THAT IS A CHANNEL THIS REPOSITORY DID NOT HAVE.
S29 found `createStrings({ loaded })` uncallable from TypeScript — TS2353 — while every one of
the repository's 1,000+ tests was green, because every one of them is JavaScript. The
declaration probes in `tools/declaration-probes/` were built for exactly that gap; the examples
are the same kind of evidence at a larger scale, because they are the consumer code a reader
will copy. So they are compiled under the same `strict` settings as `src/`.
`noEmit` is the whole reason this is a separate configuration rather than an addition to
`tsconfig.json`'s `include`. That one EMITS into `types/`, which is the artifact
library's public surface — so an example compiled through it would publish `types/examples/*`
and the port would appear to export a bookshop.
